html:
Mill Creek Culture is the label this map gives to a people of east Texas and the Red River country between about 1 and 500 CE. Where the label comes from is unclear. The best known Mill Creek culture is a different and later one: farming villages in northwest Iowa from about 1100 to 1300.

In east Texas in these centuries, archaeologists usually describe Woodland peoples who hunted, fished, gathered and made simple pottery, often grouped as the Fourche Maline culture. They lived in small settlements along rivers and buried their dead in middens and small mounds. They are widely thought to be among the ancestors of the Caddo, who built mound centres in the same country after about 800 CE. The Marksville culture lay to the east, on the lower Mississippi.
